name: BoxCast
shortDescription: A US livestreaming platform for churches and other organisations, with website embedding, social distribution, scheduling and video hosting.
suitableContexts: Churches seeking a dedicated live video platform
Teams that need website embedding and scheduled social broadcasts

pricing.summary: BoxCast’s published Standard plan is US$109 per month when billed annually, or US$119 monthly. Hardware, storage and plan suitability should be checked directly, including UK availability.

tiers.label: Standard
tiers.detail: Publishes 1080p streaming, scheduling, 90-day archive storage and seven-day support

pricing.trialDetails: BoxCast advertises a 14-day Standard trial without a card. Its published subscription terms also describe an annual commitment and a 30-day money-back guarantee.

support: Seven-day support stated on Standard plan

editorial.assessment: BoxCast is a specialist streaming option for a church that has moved beyond an informal social-stream workflow. Its public US pricing and 14-day trial make it practical to evaluate, but a UK church should ask for its applicable contract, support arrangements and complete production setup.
bestFor: Churches wanting a dedicated stream embedded on their website
Teams prepared to test a repeatable Sunday broadcast workflow
strengths: Website, social and archive workflow in one specialist product
limitations: Ask about UK availability, applicable data terms and hardware requirements

procurementVerdict.problem: Churches wanting a dedicated stream embedded on their website

longForm.verdict: BoxCast is worth trialling when livestreaming has become a regular ministry service rather than an occasional social broadcast. The useful comparison is not simply monthly price: test it with the church’s real encoder, internet connection, volunteers and destinations before relying on it for Sundays.

decisionLens.heading: A dependable stream begins before the platform.
decisionLens.text: A platform can schedule, distribute and host video, but it cannot repair weak venue upload speed, poor audio or an unclear operator handover. Treat the trial as a full service rehearsal and document who does what when something fails.

sections.heading: Dedicated distribution and archive
sections.question: What does a church gain beyond going live directly to a social network?
paragraphs: BoxCast combines a website player, social distribution, scheduling, archive storage and viewing analytics. That can give the church a clearer home for its service than relying only on a social feed.

The right question is whether those features solve a real operating issue. A small team that mainly needs a simple YouTube stream may not need a separate platform, while a team needing a managed website destination and regular archive may value it.

userFeedback.summary: This profile does not assign an independent review score. The assessment is based on BoxCast’s public Standard pricing and its house-of-worship product information.
themes: The published trial supports a practical reliability test.
Costs need to be considered alongside the production equipment and operating workload.
userFeedback.caveat: Supplier material describes product capabilities and US commercial terms; it does not establish suitability or availability for every UK church.

faq.question: Does BoxCast offer a free trial?
faq.answer: BoxCast advertises a 14-day trial of its Standard plan without a card. Confirm the current eligibility and cancellation terms before starting.

faq.question: How much is BoxCast?
faq.answer: The published Standard plan is US$109 per month billed annually, or US$119 month to month. Other needs may require different plans or equipment.

faq.question: Can a UK church use BoxCast?
faq.answer: Ask BoxCast to confirm UK availability and local contractual terms before treating its US pricing as a UK quote.
